title: What The Balalaika Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Russian philosophy absurdist melancholy
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The balalaika is a triangular-bodied Russian string affair
Three sides, three strings, one instrument that needs no compare
The shape makes certain structural and acoustic compromises
That somehow produce a sound that continuously surprises

[Pre-Chorus]
I held a balalaika once in a museum gift shop in Melbourne
Put it down very carefully and backed away — that's my concern

[Chorus]
What does the balalaika know that I don't know?
It knows the depth of winter when the Volga's under snow
What does the balalaika know in a Russian night?
It knows that melancholy played with virtuosity is right
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The prima balalaika is the highest and the smallest
The contrabass is the largest and arguably the tallest
An orchestra of balalaikas is a thing that genuinely exists
And once you've heard one you understand what magic is

[Bridge]
There's a sad Russian song inside the instrument right now
Waiting for the right musician who remembers how
The tsar is gone, the Soviet is gone, the winter stays
The balalaika has outlasted every single phase

[Outro]
Balalaika knows… the winter always comes back… balalaika knows
That's my boy
